int_name: N DARIEN ST & W LYCOMING ST

result.summary: The image depicts a residential intersection with row houses and narrow streets. While sidewalks are present, the environment lacks essential safety features such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, and traffic control signage.

hazards.name: Missing Crosswalks
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks fails to provide a designated and visible path for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The corners lack ADA-compliant ramps, making the crossing difficult for people with mobility impairments.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners block the view between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-style markings to improve pedestrian visibility and driver awareness.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install concrete curb ramps with tactile warnings at all four corners.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Implement parking restrictions near the intersection to clear sightlines.

result.summary: This residential street provides basic sidewalks on both sides but lacks any formal pedestrian crossing infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or curb ramps. The roadway surface is in poor condition with significant patching and potholes, and parked vehicles along both curbs create potential sightline obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Degraded Roadway Surface
hazards.description: Large patches and potholes in the center of the street create tripping hazards and may cause unpredictable vehicle movements.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground and mid-ground of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Visibility
hazards.description: Continuous street parking on both sides of the narrow roadway obscures pedestrians, especially children, from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs where vehicles are parked

hazards.name: Absence of Controlled Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or traffic control devices, forcing pedestrians to cross unprotected.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at intersections to define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at all crossing points to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting at Intersections
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: This residential street features narrow travel lanes and continuous sidewalks, which naturally helps to calm traffic speeds. However, the intersection lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps, creating barriers for accessibility and safety.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalk
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to designate a safe crossing area for pedestrians at the intersection.

hazards.name: Missing curb ramps
hazards.description: The absence of curb ramps creates a significant physical barrier for individuals using wheelchairs, strollers, or other mobility aids.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corner can block the visibility between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install ladder or zebra-style pavement markings to clearly define the pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Construct concrete curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces at all crossing points.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by narrow sidewalks with physical obstructions and a complete lack of marked crossings or pedestrian-specific traffic controls. Visibility is limited by parked vehicles and building placement at the corner, creating a moderately hostile environment for walking.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is located in the middle of a narrow sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to navigate a very tight space or step into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image on the sidewalk in front of the grocery store.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts as drivers may not expect pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along the right side of the street may hide pedestrians from oncoming traffic, particularly at the corner.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint zebra-style crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and alert drivers to crossing locations.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians by moving the waiting area past parked cars.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Utility Relocation
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalk and move utility poles to ensure a continuous, unobstructed path for all users, including those with mobility aids.
